lens: quality: is it audibly better for a League-level player in a real fight
build: HEAD 10dcf8ba9 (f4db1c56d + runtime evidence), dev server :5190, Chrome fake audio output

items.evidence: I ran probe_audio_runtime match myself (300 s, rift_coop, default settings) on 2 seeds. Lisvel s21: PASS, master I -18.33 LUFS, kit 73.3 %, library 20.0 % (round 1: -20.16 / 46.2 %). Odrum s7: PASS, -17.75 LUFS, kit 86.8 %. The announcer gate holds (+10.9 / +6.9 dB over sfx p99). The top library cues c_monster_fall, c_cast_big and c_hit_magic are out of the top 6. The engineer's numbers reproduce within 0.1 dB. The mechanism is industry standard: own kit +1 dB, camp monsters -3 dB, mix trim 3.0 -> 3.5 dB, fight-heat sfx ease 3 dB, calm ambience lift 3 dB. Caveat: Lisvel's own auto (attack_hit plus swing) is 66 % of heard sfx energy on s21, and on Odrum s7 f_odrum_a1_hit alone is 29.8 %.

items.id: b hit transients and dark hits
items.evidence: The 3 ms gate is met on a sample-peak metric: a short tick at the onset now holds the absolute peak sample. The body's envelope did not move. On the 32 shared kit hits, median sample rise went 7.8 -> 2.1 ms, but the 2 ms RMS envelope rise is 7.6 -> 7.6 ms. Examples (sample / 2 ms RMS): burdam_attack_hit 52 -> 1.0 / 32.9 -> 31.6 ms, lisvel_hit 43 -> 1.0 / 25.4 -> 25.3 ms, tunlan_hit 80.9 -> 0.5 / 13.0 -> 17.9 ms (worse). The tick is audible: 1 ms RMS in the first 3 ms rises 4-8 dB (tunlan_hit -15.5 -> -7.4, lisvel_hit -15.3 -> -10.9 dBFS). So the attack gains a click, but the blow does not hit harder or sooner. Dark hits: none of the 7 I re-measured changed in HF. dunsom_attack_hit 0.00 / 0.00 %, dunsom_hit 0.8 / 0.09, tunlan_hit 1.4 / 0.005, ulkro_attack_hit 5.8 / 0.02, hesmi_attack_hit 4.9 / 0.008, lisvel_attack_hit 10.1 / 0.14, nurrow_hit 2.2 / 3.6 (2-6 kHz / >6 kHz). All are recorded as by design or identity-exempt in sfx2c_onset_hf_record.json. 7-8 shared ability hits are exempt from the snap gate.

All 32 cues exist, are bound, are 3-take mono files, and fire in my captures. On Odrum s7, f_odrum_ult_hit is 1.2 % and f_odrum_a1_hit is 29.8 % of heard sfx; Lisvel s21 has lisvel_a1_hit 1.1 %. Within a kit they differ clearly from the shared hit (third-octave distance ult vs shared 10-23 dB). Across fighters, though, they lose the identity the shared hits had. Ult pairs under the lane's own 8 dB identity bar: 36 of 120 (min 3.3 dB: ervet/rishal; burdam/dunsom 3.8, tunlan/dunsom 3.8, ardit/burdam 4.1, odrum/marund 4.2). Heavy pairs: 42 of 120. Shared hits: 2 of 120. They are also dark, built on a common boom template: median centroid ult 541 Hz, heavy 604 Hz, shared hit 1300 Hz. 24 of 32 impacts are under the lane's HF floors, e.g. burdam ult 2-6 kHz 0.9 % (its shared hit 24.5 %), hesmi ult 0.2 / 0.03 %, vashil ult 0.3 %. Loudness, decoded and K-weighted, unity mono upmix: ult about +0.9 LU over the shared hit and heavy about +0.3. These cues are mono, though, and the engine's StereoPanner equal-power law puts a mono source 3 dB down whenever pan != 0 (stereo sources pass at unity). So off-centre, an ult lands about 2 LU under the light ability hit it replaced. Take variation is low: TF similarity 0.955-0.985, median about 0.975. A Burdam or Dunsom ult now reads as the same low boom, and it is the quietest-feeling blow of the kit when panned. That is the opposite of the LoL gauge, where the ult impact is the kit's loudest and most signature sound.

Decoded, as heard (file + gain): ui_shop_buy rise 45.1 -> 1.2 ms and 2-6 kHz 2.7 -> 15.3 %; ui_shop_sell 52.5 -> 1.5 ms; ui_shop_undo 89.9 -> 1.6 ms. New ui_shop_open -25.4 / 1.2 ms, ui_shop_close -26.3 / 1.1 ms, ui_ping_wheel -29.4 / 2.4 ms, ui_shop_denied -24.4 / 1.2 ms, ui_rank_up -25.1 / 2.2 ms. They sit on a coherent ladder between buy -24 and tab -28.2. Wiring checked in src/ui/hud (index.tsx toggle, close and Esc; shop.tsx Close and search Escape; dialbar.tsx gleam button and right-click sell; world.tsx wheel open edge). Residuals: the door and wheel cues are dark for 'crisp' (2-6 kHz 0.6-1.5 %, >6 kHz about 0). ui_hover is -47.4 LUFS-M heard, 20 dB under click, and was kept unchanged: likely inaudible under music. Right-click sell plays shop_sell before the sim accepts. dialbar.tsx:509 fires when shopOpen is true even if canShop is false, so away from base with the shop open the player hears a sale that did not happen.

audio/cues/kits_c.py IMPW = (0.15, 0.9) restored, and TAKE_TAU_MIN {'f_odrum_hit': 0.5}. Decoded f_odrum_hit takes are 0.194 / 0.175 / 0.176 s, inside the window. The re-take kept the cue's character: 2-6 kHz 24.2 %, rise 6.4 ms (exempt).

Only w_glimwick_bolt changed this round. On the lane's own sfx_ab.tf_sim it moved 0.960 -> 0.910. On my raw log-STFT (0.5 s, 1024/256) it moved 0.990 -> 0.985, so the takes still sound close. The other six Wick cues are byte-identical in measure to round 1 and already passed then (0.778-0.956). Small but real.

problems.what: The per-ability impacts (SFX-4) share one dark boom template: ults and heavies are confusable across fighters and lose the material brightness of the hits they replace
problems.evidence: Cross-fighter third-octave distance under the lane's 8 dB identity bar: ults 36/120 pairs (min 3.3 dB, ervet/rishal; burdam/dunsom 3.8), heavies 42/120, shared hits 2/120. Median centroid: ult 541 Hz, heavy 604 Hz, shared 1300 Hz. 24/32 impacts are under the HF floors (2-6 kHz >= 4 %, >6 kHz >= 0.6 %); burdam ult 0.9 % vs its shared hit 24.5 %. On Odrum s7, f_odrum_a1_hit (2-6 kHz 0.8 %, >6 kHz 0.11 %) is 29.8 % of heard sfx. snap_gate checks rise and laptop loss for the impacts but not identity or HF.
problems.fix: Run the 8 dB identity gate across all ult hits and all heavy hits as two groups, and apply the HF floors to them. Voice each ult from the fighter's own material crack and signature at the top, not a shared pitch-dropping boom, and keep the boom as a sub-layer. Raise take variation to TF <= 0.95.

problems.what: The 3 ms snap is met on the sample peak only: the body envelope's rise is unchanged, and no dark hit gained HF
problems.evidence: 32 shared hits: 2 ms RMS rise median 7.6 -> 7.6 ms while the sample-peak rise went 7.8 -> 2.1 ms. tunlan_hit 2 ms RMS went 13.0 -> 17.9 ms. The 7 dark hits' 2-6 kHz and >6 kHz shares are unchanged to the second decimal. Per-cue reasons are recorded, so the item is closed on paper, not by ear.
problems.fix: Gate the rise on a 1-2 ms RMS envelope, not the sample peak, and move the body's peak forward (a shorter attack on the body layer), not only a tick in front of it.

problems.what: Mono impacts lose 3 dB against stereo cues whenever they are panned
problems.evidence: f_*_ult_hit and f_*_aN_hit are 1-channel, and the shared hits are 2-channel. src/audio/index.ts:1268 inserts a StereoPanner only when pan != 0. The WebAudio equal-power law for a mono input gives cos(pi/4) = -3 dB at pan near 0, while a stereo input passes at unity. Decoded K-weighted: ult +0.9 LU over the shared hit unpanned, so about -2 LU panned.
problems.fix: Compensate mono spatial cues by +3 dB (or by a pan-law-matched gain) in the panner branch, or render the impacts in stereo. Then re-check the ult's as-heard level is above the shared hit's by 1.5-3 dB.

problems.what: Right-click sell plays the sell sound when the sim will reject the sale
problems.evidence: src/ui/hud/dialbar.tsx:509: sound.play('shop_sell') when shopOpen.value || canShop. With the shop open away from base (RIFT shopAccess base_or_dead) the sale is refused, but the player hears a sale.
problems.fix: Play on the sim's confirmation (the sale's event or the inventory change), or gate the sound on canShop alone.

problems.what: ui_hover is about 20 dB under the rest of the UI ladder
problems.evidence: As heard -47.4 LUFS-M against click -27.4 and tab -28.2. It was kept unchanged as 'level-matched'.
problems.fix: Lift ui_hover to about -36 to -38 LUFS-M (a soft tick 8-10 dB under the click), or record why it is meant to be near-silent.

budgets: No geometry, texture or GPU change, so triangles, draws and shader programs are unchanged (audio only). Memory: the new cues add about 10.3 MB decoded PCM in all (64 impact takes plus 3 UI cues). A 10-fighter match loads about 6.5 MB, against a 135 MB RIFT margin (2865 of 3000). The claim's 'no memory change' is slightly inaccurate, but this is within budget. probe_match_memory was not re-run by either side. probe_audio_runtime match: my 2 fresh captures PASS (Lisvel s21 -18.33 LUFS / 73.3 %, Odrum s7 -17.75 / 86.8 %). I did not run the frame timing (final idle gate only). The engineer reports the full probe suite was not re-run after the fixture fix.
notes: Quality lens. Round-1 references are the decoded files at 69519e8f2, extracted to my scratchpad. All measurements are numpy on ffmpeg-decoded audio: 1/3-octave band distance and HF shares (the lane's definitions), K-weighted momentary max, sample-peak and RMS-envelope rise, and STFT TF similarity. Mono files were corrected for ffmpeg's -3 dB upmix. The lane is better than round 1 where it mattered most: the live mix gate now passes reproducibly, and the shop actions are crisp and wired. It is not clearly at par. SFX-4 delivered per-ability impacts that are dark, template-alike booms (36-42 of 120 cross-fighter pairs under the lane's own identity bar). The snap is a sample-peak tick rather than a harder, sooner blow. In a real fight, ults should be the loudest and most signature blow. Here a panned ult lands under the light hit it replaced and sounds like other fighters' ults. No sensitivity or originality issue: all cues are original procedural synthesis, with no library or LoL material. Fail: one major problem (SFX-4 identity and darkness), and the score 7.2 is under par 7.5.
